messages.text: The policy library suite passed: 1,186 tests, with two skipped. The checkpoint is compiling and behavior preserving so far. I’m doing the final format check, then I’ll hand back the changed files and the remaining DTO work for the parent’s commit.
I handed the parent a compiling checkpoint across four files. The policy library suite passed (1,186 tests); the durable Output DTO, execution wiring, and golden remain to be completed.

I’ll build on the committed checkpoint. I’ll first map the fields that policy projection reads from a composed report, then define a flow-owned JSON DTO around stable event, origin, and witness identities. I’ll keep the decoder responsible for rejecting corrupt persisted rows.

I found an existing flow composition fixture that can produce two origins at one sink. I’m using it for the DTO round-trip test. The first DTO layer will encode stable event and locator rows plus origin classes and witness references, then validate every index and ordering rule on decode.

The flow DTO now round-trips a real composed report with two origins and retained witness steps. The test exposed a partial witness on one origin, so the DTO records that completeness state; publication will reject open anchors later. I’m tightening the decoder’s value checks next.

The DTO test passes with two origins, a retained witness, and a corrupt witness-index check. The current DTO still needs authored closures, frontier-source metadata, store crossings, and barrier evidence before policy can use it as a durable prefix. I’m finishing lint on this compiling slice.

The DTO now validates sink identities and class names against the current taint plan, and the two-origin test passes after that change. I’m at a compiling checkpoint. I’ll run the final format, lint, and drift checks, then hand back the changed files near the turn limit.

The focused DTO test still passes after I narrowed the completeness helper to its report-side meaning. It does not yet decide publication for an entire Output unit; store seeding, diagnostics, and execution work still need checks in the policy prefix. I’m finishing the checkpoint checks now.

I handed the parent a compiling checkpoint with the flow-owned JSON DTO and a passing two-origin witness round-trip test. Output-unit wiring, remaining evidence fields, the golden, and full gates remain.
I’ll inspect the committed DTO against the report fields and projection code, then finish the stored evidence and use it in the per-anchor unit path.

The current DTO stores sink and origin labels plus witness paths, but the composed projection also reads frontier carriers, authored closures, barrier evidence and store crossings. I’m tracing those types before adding fields so a reused row carries the same evidence as a fresh report.

The DTO now retains authored call closures, path quality and report work counters; the focused round-trip still passes. I’m adding a structured frontier carrier row next, because both policy and public witness projection use that carrier when a source was found outside the compiled plan.

Store crossings now have structured artifact and call keys plus a witness path reference. I’m extending the same product with barrier checks and strict/lenient pair reports, then I’ll verify the complete DTO before wiring the unit loop.

The flow crate compiles and the focused DTO test passes. Wiring reuse exposes a decision point: projection currently consumes live report handles, while the stored DTO has stable locators. I’ll hand back the two viable ways to bridge them with the relevant call sites.
Checkpoint handed to the parent with the changed file, passing checks, and the projection decision needed to continue.
I’ll start at the flow boundary: make the carrier rows safe for deeply nested keys, then check what the shared projector needs from the rows.
The carrier conversion now uses an explicit stack in both directions. The focused test is rebuilding its dependencies; once it finishes, I’ll check the row access needed by the projector.

The iterative carrier conversion, stable event-key reconstruction, and focused round-trip test pass. This is a compiling checkpoint; the shared projector and unit loop still need the row-facing refactor.
Compiling checkpoint handed to the parent. The flow boundary checks pass; shared projection and Output unit wiring remain.
I’ll trace the composed projection path and identify the live fields it reads, then move that path to the validated Output rows. Fresh and reused anchors will need to enter the same projector.

I found and fixed two DTO spellings that would change public witness output: dispatch boundaries used Debug text, and end summary gaps used title case. The rows now use the projector’s labels. The flow checks pass; the projector and unit wiring are still in progress.
Checkpoint handed to the parent. The DTO now exposes the fields needed by the stable row projector, and flow checks pass. The projector and Output unit wiring remain unfinished.
I’ll add the RQL entry point for decoded Output rows, then route fresh composed anchors through it. I’ll keep the existing ICFG report projector in place while checking public output parity.

The row based witness-step renderer now matches the live renderer’s fields, including symbols, zero facts, evidence and boundary labels. RQL clippy is still running; I’ll resolve anything it reports before continuing the projector.
The composed RQL path now encodes each fresh sink site into an Output row before public projection. ICFG still uses its report path. I’m checking the existing policy goldens next for output drift.
The existing Rust declared-storage golden is still building. This run should show whether encoding fresh composed sites before public projection preserves its expected output.
The Rust stored-request golden and its forced-ICFG parity test passed with the new public row projection. The composed flow golden is rebuilding now; it covers more witness and diagnostic shapes.

The composed flow golden passed, as did the Rust declared-storage golden and its parity test. I also removed an unnecessary live-source lookup from the row projector. I’m formatting and checking the final diff before handing back this checkpoint.
The checkpoint is with the parent. Fresh composed sites now use stable Output rows for public projection, and the focused goldens pass. Policy projection and Output unit reuse remain unfinished.
I’ll move policy finding projection onto the stable Output rows first, then connect the per-anchor unit loop. I’ll check the current checkpoint and projection code before editing.

The existing policy projector carries live finding and origin references through grouping, certainty, witnesses, and store evidence. I’m replacing those references at the grouping boundary so the downstream projector can use the same decoded rows for both fresh and reused anchors.

I found one missing piece in the durable barrier rows: the rendered note uses source mapping details and a procedure/value label that the current DTO does not carry. I’m adding those scalar fields to the row so reuse can render the note without loading the original artifact.

The crossing row also needs call site locators. It currently keeps durable call IDs, but rendering a reused witness from those IDs would require loading artifacts. I’m carrying the selected write/read call locators through the composed crossing and into the JSON row.

The call locators now travel with composed store crossings, and the Output row records them. I’m waiting for the touched flow tests and policy crate to compile before continuing the projection wiring.

The compile check passed. The new row helpers are still unused until policy projection is switched over, so I’m running the existing composed store golden now to catch any mismatch in the richer row encoding.
The focused golden is still in its build/link stage. The code compiles; I’m letting this check finish so the checkpoint includes a real composed store run.

The composing store golden and the flow DTO round trip both pass. Clippy is clean after boxing the new locators in the `Hop::Store` variant. I’m stopping at this compiling checkpoint near the turn limit so the parent can commit it; the policy row projector and unit loop still need wiring.
Checkpoint handed to the parent. The lane compiles, clippy and formatting pass, and the focused golden and DTO round trip pass. Policy projection from Output rows and the per-anchor unit loop remain.

I’ll map the remaining policy projection inputs to the Output rows, starting with store seed evidence and sanitizer declines. Then I’ll connect the row projector for composed findings and validate the affected paths.

The Output row now carries writer and origin locations for seeded reads, plus sanitizer declines matched to retained witness steps. The policy projector is still on live findings; I’m validating this DTO checkpoint before switching that path.
Clippy passes for the DTO changes. The focused composed store golden is rebuilding the root test binary; I’ll inspect its result and then hand back a compiling checkpoint if the turn limit is close.

Checkpoint handed to the parent. The Output row now records store seed and sanitizer decline evidence; the focused golden, compile check, and clippy pass. Policy projection from rows and the unit loop remain.
I’ll merge the latest `origin/master` into the lane first and preserve the provider split. Then I’ll continue the row projector against the merged code.

The merge is blocked by the sandbox: `git fetch` cannot write the lane’s `FETCH_HEAD`. The lane is clean at `26ed7a342f`. I asked the parent to perform the merge, as offered, before I continue the projector work.

I’ll continue from the merged head and focus on policy projection from Output rows. I’ll first confirm the merged code’s call sites and the current row fields, then replace the live finding references in the composed path.

The merged lane is clean at `af4b5d4757`. I found that the Output crossing row still lacks the endpoint, channel, and upstream witness evidence used by policy projection. No files changed this turn; those fields need to be added before the row projector can replace the live path.
I’ll extend the crossing row with the policy provenance it needs, then move the composed policy projector to consume those rows. I’ll keep the new fields SQL-readable and validate them on decode.
The crossing DTO shape is in place and compiles, but its policy provenance records are not populated yet. I handed the checkpoint to the parent with the remaining projection and unit-loop work.

I’ll populate each crossing’s policy metadata from the compiled store ends, then add decode checks. I’ll keep the records keyed by policy and source endpoint because a shared composed batch can serve more than one policy.
The crossing policy metadata now populates and validates, and the lane compiles. I handed the checkpoint to the parent. The row policy projector, unit loop, and golden remain.
I’ll wire the composed policy projector to the stored Output rows first, then use that path for per-anchor execution. I’ll check the current call sites and row fields before editing.

The stable row already carries the site, origins, witnesses, store crossings, barrier pairs, and sanitizer declines. I’ll keep the ICFG projector as it is and move composed policy findings onto a row-specific path, using the existing policy identities and limits.
I’m resuming from the uncommitted row projector edits. I’ll compile that checkpoint first, fix any errors, then continue connecting it to the composed policy call site.
The new row helpers compile, but they are not connected yet, so they produce unused-code warnings. I’ll leave this checkpoint clean and identify the remaining connection work for the parent.
Checkpoint handed back to the parent. The Output-row projection helpers compile and are formatted, but the composed projector and Output units are not yet wired.
I’ll attach each origin to the report that owns its witness indices, then connect the composed policy projector to the validated rows. I’ll keep the ICFG route as it is.

The owning-report association is now in place for witness lookup, and the policy crate compiles. I’m adding the row grouping step next so the projector can handle sources from both ordinary Output rows and nested barrier reports.
I handed back a compiling checkpoint with the row grouping changes. The composed projector, Output units, and golden remain to be completed.
I’ll connect the policy projection to Output rows now. I’ll build the row projector around the existing grouping helpers, then switch composed batches to it while leaving ICFG on its current path.

The composed route now calls the row projector and compiles. I’m removing the temporary dead-code annotations, then I’ll check that persisted rows retain the evidence needed for strict barriers and store crossings.
The existing declared-store golden is building now. The row projector compiles; this golden will check whether the public finding and evidence rendering still match after the projection switch.
The golden build is still compiling the analyzer dependency and has not reached the test. I’ll wait for its result before changing projection behavior further.
The golden build has reached the policy and root crates. Once it finishes, I’ll use the first diff or failure to correct the row projection without reblessing the expected file.

The deployed store golden passes. The barrier golden fails its ICFG versus composition evidence comparison for `bounded-unknown`; I’m capturing that diff so I can identify the field that diverged before changing the projector.

The evidence rows match until the bounded barrier-note limit: composition retains five more notes than the live ICFG path, and both mark notes truncated. The note cap currently charges Rust allocation capacity, which changes after JSON decoding. I’m preserving the exact diff and handing the cap decision back before changing that shared behavior.

I handed back the row projector and the barrier parity failure with the evidence and decision options. The deployed store golden passes; the bounded barrier case needs a decision on stable note charging before I continue.

I’ll make barrier-note admission charge content bytes in both the live and row paths, then rerun the parity golden. I’ll inspect any changed golden lines before blessing them and proceed to the Output unit loop once parity holds.

ICFG and composition now agree. One existing golden case differs because the content-based cap retains a different bounded set of notes. I’ll bless that case, inspect its full diff for any other changes, and then run the remaining note-count checks.

The cap fix is complete: ICFG and composition now retain the same notes, the policy library tests pass, and the blessed golden changes only the bounded note arrays from 54 to 59 entries. I found one boundary the Output loop cannot cross without a contract decision: warm reuse has stable rows, while the public outcome and MCP registry currently accept only live analysis results.
The barrier cap now uses content bytes, and ICFG and composition agree. I handed back the audited golden change and a decision needed for registering reused Output rows in MCP.
I’ll trace the taint result registry and its readers first, then wire composed results through the stable rows before building the per-anchor unit loop.

The registry’s query reader is concentrated in RQL’s taint operator. It currently resolves a retained plan/report pair for an exact procedure root, then projects it. I’m adapting that registration to accept the stable rows and use the existing row projector, while preserving the ICFG branch.

The policy outcome now carries the same validated Output rows used for fresh composition projection, while retained live analyses stay on the ICFG branch. I’m wiring those rows through RQL registration and the taint query reader next.

The row transport is compiling through the policy and RQL crates. The root test build is still running; once it finishes I’ll fix any type errors, then exercise the MCP registration path before moving to the unit loop.

evidence.user_prompt_tail: Parent: committed and pushed as 185624ef7b. Decision on the public outcome: yes, carry the stable Output rows in PolicyBatchOutcome for composed anchors, fresh and reused alike (the same rows), and have MCP register composed taint results from those rows; live ProductionTaintAnalysisResult stays only for ICFG runs. That keeps one path: a fresh composed anchor is encoded to rows before it is registered, so fresh and warm registrations cannot differ. Audit every MCP consumer of a registered taint result (searchtools_service.rs ~2750 and whatever reads the registry later: witness or path retrieval, explanations, related locations) and make each answer from the rows; if one needs data the rows lack, add it to the rows rather than keeping a live-only side path. Then the UnitSlice, receipts, merge and seal, the golden (cold, warm reuse, one edited remote source adding a second origin, a store-channel writer edit, two temp roots) and the gates, including suite_mcp_cli since MCP registration changes. Same stop rule.
